rows.title: Monetary Policy
rows.figure: Fed Dec hike ~87% for 25bp / ~13% for 50bp, no pause priced (CME FedWatch via Reuters, Nov 11 NY); ECB Dec ~92%; BoJ Dec ~84%; BoE Dec ~67%; BoC Dec ~34%; BoE 4.00%, RBA 4.85%
rows.read: Federal Reserve officials spent the day talking up faster rate rises, so bets grew on a half-point December hike rather than a quarter point. That pulls US rates further ahead of almost everyone, which lifted the dollar against every major currency. Hikes from Europe and Japan are expected too, but already priced.

rows.title: Growth
rows.figure: UK Q3 GDP Thu 1:00 AM CT, fcst +0.7% q/q; euro-area Q3 GDP 2nd estimate Fri 4:00 AM CT; Australia new home loans −15.5% q/q in Q3
rows.read: No major growth figures landed on Wednesday. The US economy still looks firmer than Australia's, Canada's or New Zealand's, a split that favours the dollar. UK growth figures overnight are the next big read.

rows.title: Inflation
rows.figure: US Oct CPI +0.4% m/m (fcst +0.3%), core +0.3% (fcst +0.2%), 4% y/y; US PPI Fri 7:30 AM CT fcst +0.4% m/m; Japan PPI Wed 5:50 PM CT fcst 6.5% y/y; Brent high ~$94.2 Wed
rows.read: US inflation is running at about twice the Fed's goal, and Fed officials now say it is spreading beyond energy. Oil's rise on Wednesday adds to that worry. That keeps the Fed hiking, which supports the dollar and weighs on gold.

rows.title: Risk Sentiment
rows.read: US stocks rallied, so there was little demand for safe havens despite more tanker attacks near Hormuz. The franc and the yen were among the day's biggest losers against the dollar. Gulf news is still the main thing that could change the mood fast.

rows.title: Terms of Trade
rows.figure: Brent ~$92.5 at 2:26 PM CT (high ~$94.2; Tue settle $91.49), WTI ~$86.3 (high ~$88.2); OPEC+ Oct output 41.2M b/d (+2.04M); Brent $116.72 at the Oct 30 close
rows.read: Oil rose as Iran hardened its stance and tanker attacks went on, though talk of direct US–Iran talks trimmed the gain late in the day. Dearer oil helps the Canadian dollar and weighs on Japan and the euro area. OPEC's output is close to pre-war levels, which caps how far prices can run.

rows.title: Positioning
rows.figure: CFTC Nov 3: hedge funds for USD, JPY, AUD, GBP; against NZD, CAD, EUR; 4-week change NZD −22K, EUR −34K contracts; next report Friday
rows.read: Hedge funds lean toward the dollar and the yen and against the kiwi, the Canadian dollar and the euro. The dollar's rise has gone with most of those bets, though the large bet on the yen is losing money as it weakens. The next weekly report is due Friday.

rows.title: Fiscal
rows.figure: US 10-year auction Nov 10: $42B at 5.020%, bid-to-cover 2.46 (6-auction avg 2.60); 10-year ~4.98% at Tuesday's close; bond market shut Nov 11; $25B 30-year auction Thu 12:00 PM CT
rows.read: Weak demand at US government bond sales this week pushed long-term borrowing costs up, as buyers asked for more pay to hold US debt. That supports the dollar for now but is a worry if it spreads. A 30-year bond sale on Thursday is the next check.
